Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.metaDescription: What personal data POPS (“More than just sport”) processes, why and on what legal basis, who receives it, how long it is kept and what your rights are.
Privacy.intro: POPS (“More than just sport”) is a non-profit project. This page explains what personal data we process, why and on what legal basis, who we share it with, how long we keep it and what your rights are. We collect as little data as possible and do not track users.

controller.title: Who is responsible for your data
controller.body: The controller of your personal data is the non-profit association that runs POPS:

processing.title: What we process, why and on what basis
processing.intro: The legal bases are those of Articles 6 and 9 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

browsing.title: Browsing the site
browsing.body: The map and the pages open without an account. To limit request rates and stop abuse, the server uses your IP address in memory only and does not record it. We keep no access log of IP addresses.
browsing.basis: Basis: legitimate interest in keeping the site available and secure (Art. 6(1)(f)).

analytics.title: Visit statistics and errors
analytics.body: We use self-hosted, cookieless analytics (Umami). It records the page visited (without the parameters in its address, except the campaign tags utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content and utm_term on the first page of a visit that starts from a link carrying them, which tell us which post or campaign a visit came from), the referring site, the type of browser, operating system and device, the language, and an approximate country and city derived from the IP address, which is not stored. We also record the kind of some actions — for example that someone asked for directions, sent a contribution or opened a share sheet — without who did it or which facility, training, check-in or network it concerned. If an error occurs in your browser, our self-hosted GlitchTip receives the error message, the page address (which, on the map, includes the map's centre) and the browser type, with no data from your profile. We build no profiles and do not track people across sites.
analytics.basis: Basis: legitimate interest in knowing what is used and what is broken (Art. 6(1)(f)).

account.title: Account and sign-in
account.body: If you create an account: your email address (for sign-in with a one-time code), a display name, an optional city and whether you are under 18. Your date of birth, if you enter it in your profile, is used once to work out that category and is never stored. While you are signed in, we keep your browser type (user agent) with the session, but not your IP address.
account.basis: Basis: contract — the <terms>Terms of use</terms> you accept when you sign in (Art. 6(1)(b)).

signInProviders.title: Signing in with {providers}
signInProviders.body: If you choose to sign in with {providers}, the service sends us your email address, whether it has verified it, and your account ID there; it may also send your name and profile picture there. We keep only the email address and the ID: they are how we recognise you the next time you sign in, until you delete your POPS profile. We do not store the name or the picture: you choose your POPS display name yourself. We do not receive your password, your contacts or your friends list, we never post anything on your behalf, and we keep no keys to your account with the service.
signInProviders.basis: Basis: contract — the <terms>Terms of use</terms> you accept when you sign in (Art. 6(1)(b)). Signing in with {providers} is your choice: you can always sign in with an email code instead.

contributions.title: Contributions and points
contributions.body: When you add or verify a facility, report its condition or upload a photo, we record the contribution with your account id in the change log, and the points in the points ledger. Facility data becomes part of the <openData>open data</openData> under the ODbL licence. Photos are published after a moderator approves them and with all metadata, including GPS, removed; a rejected or taken-down photo is deleted for good.

location.title: Location
location.body: If you allow it, your browser uses your location to show the map and the nearest facilities around you; this happens in the browser itself and the coordinates are not sent to the server. When you contribute, report a problem or check in at a session, the coordinates arrive with the form; the server works out the distance to the facility and stores only that, never the coordinates themselves.
location.basis: Basis: contract and legitimate interest in protecting points and data from abuse (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f)).

passport.title: Public passport and leaderboards
passport.body: Only if you make your passport public yourself are your display name and city shown on the passport, with your badges, totals and streaks, and on the leaderboards (including “Who plays” with your number of trainings and minutes), in campaigns and in divisions. When and where you played is never published.
passport.basis: Basis: consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), which you withdraw by making your passport private.

sessions.title: Group sessions
sessions.body: Signing up for a session, your place on the waiting list and your check-ins are stored with your account. The session organiser sees the display names of those signed up; the public page shows only how many. If you organise a session, your display name is shown on its public page.

training.title: Training log
training.body: Sport, date and time, duration and, optionally, distance, elevation, facility and a note. Only you can see the log; if your passport is public, your number of trainings and minutes count towards the “Who plays” board. There are no Strava, Garmin or Apple Health connections yet, so we collect no GPS routes and no heart-rate data. If we add them, we will ask for separate explicit consent and describe here what we collect, from where and for how long.
training.basis: Basis: contract (Art. 6(1)(b)); for health data — explicit consent only (Art. 9(2)(a)).

mail.title: Emails
mail.body: We send the sign-in code, session confirmations and reminders and notices if a session is cancelled, emails about moderation decisions and — only if you subscribe — a weekly digest for your city.
mail.basis: Basis: contract (Art. 6(1)(b)); for the digest — consent, which you withdraw with the unsubscribe link in every email.

reports.title: Facility problem reports
reports.body: Reports of broken equipment, missing lighting or a bad surface are anonymous — we ask for no name, email or account.
reports.basis: Basis: legitimate interest in accurate facility data (Art. 6(1)(f)).

notices.title: Content notices
notices.body: The <form>notice form</form> records the address of the content, the kind of problem, your explanation and — only if you enter them — a name and email, so we can confirm receipt and tell you the decision. Your IP address is not recorded.
notices.basis: Basis: legal obligation under Article 16 of the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065) — Art. 6(1)(c).

moderation.title: Moderation and accountability
moderation.body: We record which moderator took which decision and when, and for a refusal the reason, which we email to the author. When an administrator opens an account in the admin panel, that is recorded too: who, whose account and when.
moderation.basis: Basis: legal obligation under Article 17 of the Digital Services Act and legitimate interest in every decision and every access being checkable (Art. 6(1)(c) and (f)).

tokens.title: Calendar and open-data keys
tokens.body: If you create them: a personal address through which your calendar follows the sessions you signed up for, and an open-data API key, of which we keep only a fingerprint (hash) — the key itself is not stored.

recipients.title: Who receives data
recipients.intro: We do not sell data and do not use it for advertising. We share it only with the following recipients, and only as far as needed:
recipients.hosting: Hetzner Online GmbH (Germany) — hosting and backups. The server and the database are in a data centre in Finland (EU); once off-server backups are switched on, encrypted copies of the database and the uploaded photos are kept in a separate Hetzner data centre in Germany (EU).
recipients.network: Cloudflare, Inc. (USA) — network protection and delivery. Every visit to the site passes through Cloudflare’s network on its way to our server, so Cloudflare processes your IP address and the requests themselves (including which pages you open) to deliver the site and protect it from attacks, and keeps technical logs of this for a limited time under its own terms. It keeps copies only of the site’s design files, fonts and icons, which are the same for everyone — never of pages, photos or anything about you.
recipients.mail: Migadu-Mail GmbH (Switzerland) — our email. The site’s messages to you (sign-in codes, session confirmations and reminders, decisions on your contributions) are sent through Migadu, so your address and their content pass through it; messages you write to us are kept in our mailbox there until we delete them — write to us if you want yours deleted.
recipients.people: People at POPS: a session organiser sees the display names of those signed up; ambassadors (volunteer moderators for their municipality) see the contributions and facility reports there; administrators can use the admin panel, and every time they open an account it is recorded.
recipients.external: External services you choose. The default map is served entirely from our own server, but if you pick an external map layer (CyclOSM, Thunderforest Transport, Tracestrack Topo), your browser loads tiles directly from that provider, and the “Directions” button opens Waze or Google Maps at the facility. They see your IP address, as they would if you visited their site.
recipients.signInProviders: {providers}, if you choose to sign in with them. The service learns that you are signing in to POPS and handles that under its own privacy policy; we send it no data about you.
recipients.noSale: Ads and partner logos on the site receive no data about you: they are shown the same to everyone, and we count neither their views nor their clicks.

transfers.title: Transfers outside the EU
transfers.body: Your data is stored in the EU. It can leave the EU through Cloudflare, whose network every visit to the site passes through and which also processes data in the United States under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; through our email provider Migadu, a Swiss company — the EU recognises Switzerland as ensuring an adequate level of data protection; and through the external services you choose yourself.

retention.title: How long we keep data
retention.account: Your account — until you delete it. You can delete it yourself from <profile>My profile</profile>: the profile, email, sessions, points, sign-ups and check-ins, training log and subscriptions go at once, and your contributions stay in the shared data anonymously, as “former user”.
retention.codes: Sign-in codes — {minutes} minutes; then they expire and are deleted automatically.
retention.sessions: Sign-in sessions, with the browser type — until you sign out or 30 days after your last visit.
retention.contributions: The change log of facility data and the moderation decisions — with no time limit, because the history of the open data must stay traceable; once your account is deleted, those records are no longer linked to you.
retention.notices: The name and email in a content notice — up to {days} days after the decision on it; the notice itself and the decision are kept as a record.
retention.logs: Records of administrators opening accounts — with no time limit, so that every such access can be checked.
retention.errors: Error reports in GlitchTip — up to 90 days.
retention.backups: Backups — of the database for up to 14 days on the server, and of the database and uploaded photos for about 8 weeks in a separate data centre, once that is switched on. A deleted account or photo disappears from them as the copies expire.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You have the right to access your data and receive a copy, to rectification, to erasure, to restriction of processing, to data portability and to object to processing based on legitimate interest. You can withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before that.
rights.self: You can do much of this yourself from <profile>My profile</profile>: change your name and city, make your passport private, unsubscribe from the digest and delete your account.
rights.ask: For anything else — for example a copy of your data — write to the address under “Who is responsible for your data” or on the <contact>Contact</contact> page. We reply within one month.
rights.complaint: You have the right to lodge a complaint with the Bulgarian Commission for Personal Data Protection (<cpdp>www.cpdp.bg</cpdp>).

cookies.title: Cookies and data in your browser
cookies.body: We use no analytics or advertising cookies, and the site sets no language cookie. When you sign in, your browser keeps a session cookie (up to 30 days) and a short-lived signed cookie (5 minutes) so we do not have to look the session up on every request. They are strictly necessary for signing in and are deleted when you sign out.
cookies.providers: If you sign in with {providers}, your browser also keeps a short signed cookie (up to 5 minutes) during the sign-in itself, which links your request to the service's answer. It is strictly necessary too.
cookies.cache: So that the map works offline, your browser caches the app's files and icons, an offline page and the map tiles you viewed last. They contain no data about you and you can clear them in your browser settings.

minors.title: Minors
minors.body: We have not set a minimum age for an account. Your date of birth, if you enter it, is used once to note whether you are under 18 and is not stored; at present that flag restricts nothing. Our age policy is under review and we will update this page when it is adopted.

automated.title: Automated decisions
automated.body: We take no decisions based solely on automated processing. Automated checks can only prompt moderators; every moderation decision is taken by a person.

sources.title: Where facility data comes from
sources.body: Facility data is based on OpenStreetMap (ODbL) and the base map on Protomaps. Community contributions are published as part of the shared <openData>open data</openData>.

changes.body: When we change this page, we update the date at its top.

Accountability.methodCondition: Condition is the most recent visitor report for each facility, not an assessment of ours. “Not reported” means nobody has reported yet.
Accountability.methodResponse: The median runs from a report being filed to a moderator's decision, over the last {days} days, taken from the decision log. Median rather than mean: one forgotten report drags a mean anywhere.

OpenData.title: Open data
OpenData.intro: The complete register of Bulgaria's public sports facilities — free to download and free to use through a documented API. No fee, no approval, and no registration to read.
OpenData.attributionNotice: Published under ODbL 1.0. Any public use requires the attribution: “© OpenStreetMap contributors + POPS community”.
OpenData.apiIntro: Documented and versioned. The addresses under /api/opendata/v1 do not change without a new version — unlike the feeds that serve our own map.
OpenData.apiAnonymousBody: The API answers without a key. The data is public — requiring registration to read public data would be a contradiction.
OpenData.apiAuthBody: A key raises the limit and nothing else. It is sent in the Authorization header only; a key in the query string ends up in every log along the way, so it is not accepted as a parameter.
OpenData.apiLimitsBody: {anon} requests per minute without a key, {keyed} with one. Every response carries RateLimit headers so you can slow down before being refused. Going over returns 429 and points at the bulk dumps — never a ban, and never a revoked key.
OpenData.apiDumpsUnmetered: The nightly dumps are not rate limited at all.
OpenData.apiParamFormat: format — one of the dataset's formats; defaults to the first.
OpenData.apiParamLimit: limit — maximum rows. Without it the whole dataset is returned, up to a safety cap.

facilities.title: Facilities
facilities.description: The complete public register: one point per facility, with sports, surface, lighting, access, provenance and the latest reported condition. It contains exactly what a visitor sees on the map — not one row more.

statsNational.title: National statistics
statsNational.description: Country-wide totals. The same query that feeds /statistika, so a figure in the downloaded file and the same figure on the site cannot drift apart.

statsMunicipalities.title: Municipality statistics
statsMunicipalities.description: Coverage per municipality, including per 10 000 residents. Municipalities with no official population figure are left empty — not zero, and not estimated.

statsSports.title: Sport statistics
statsSports.description: Facility count per sport. A multi-sport facility counts once for each of its sports.

OpenData.dumpsIntro: Every night the whole register is written out again under a version — the civil date in Sofia. Old versions stay put, so a figure cited from a particular version can still be checked later.
OpenData.dumpsRetention: The last {keep} versions are kept. If you need a version indefinitely, keep your own copy — the checksum proves it is ours.
OpenData.dumpsNone: No dumps have been published yet.
OpenData.licenseIntro: The database is published under the Open Database License 1.0 (ODbL).
OpenData.licenseAttributionBody: On any public use of this data, or of anything made from it, state:
OpenData.licenseShareAlikeBody: The ODbL is share-alike: if you publicly use an adapted version of the database, you must offer that adapted database under the ODbL as well.
OpenData.licenseProducedWorkTitle: A map, a report or an application
OpenData.licenseProducedWorkBody: Producing a map, a report or an application FROM the data does not oblige you to open that work — the obligation is on the database behind it. Attribution is required either way.
OpenData.licensePhotosBody: Photographs are not part of this database, are not covered by this licence, and are not included in these files at all.
OpenData.licensePersonalBody: No personal data appears in any file or in any API response. The exported fields are listed by name and checked automatically — a dataset does not exist until it has passed that list.
OpenData.licenseSourceBody: Some records originate from OpenStreetMap; the rest were added and verified by the public and by municipalities. The provenance is on every record, in the “source” field.
OpenData.keysIntro: A key raises the limit from {anon} to {keyed} requests per minute. It is not needed to read — the data is public.
OpenData.keysSignInRequired: Sign in to create a key.
OpenData.keysLabelHint: So you can recognise it later if you have several.
OpenData.keysCreated: Key created. It is shown only now — we store only its fingerprint and cannot recover it.
OpenData.keysLimitReached: You have reached the maximum of {max} keys. Revoke one to create another.
OpenData.keysHeaderOnly: In the Authorization header only. A key in the query string ends up in every log along the way, so the API does not accept it as a parameter.
OpenData.keysLabelLooksLikeKey: That looks like the key itself. Give it a name you could show someone — the key must not be stored here.

Podkrepi.intro: POPS is a non-profit association. The platform is free for everybody and stays that way — there are no paid features and there will not be. Your donation pays for the server, the map data and the work of verifying facilities.
Podkrepi.fundsBody: Hosting on our own server in the European Union, map layers and backups; on-the-ground verification and work with municipalities; maintaining the open data anybody can download for free.
Podkrepi.bankIntro: We accept donations by bank transfer. There is no card form on the site: payment providers load third-party scripts and tracking cookies, and our promise is the opposite — see the Privacy page.

Podkrepi.taxBody: A donation is unrequited — no service in return, no invoice, and not advertising. Where the recipient is registered for public benefit, Bulgarian law provides donor relief:
Podkrepi.taxCompanies: Companies: donations recognised as an expense up to 10% of accounting profit (art. 31 CITA).
Podkrepi.taxIndividuals: Individuals: annual tax base reduced by up to 5% (art. 22 PITA).

AdminAccounts.trainingNote: Routes and health data are not shown here — only whether they exist.

controls.title: Account controls
controls.note: Every action here only removes access or visibility, and is recorded in the log at the foot of this page. Nothing here publishes a passport or grants a consent.
controls.unsuspendConfirm: Lift the suspension? The member will be able to sign in again. Their passport stays private until they publish it themselves.
controls.adminNote: An admin account cannot be suspended or erased from here: the role comes from the ADMIN_EMAILS list — remove the address there.
controls.suspendNote: The member is signed out of every device at once and cannot sign back in. Their passport becomes private and leaves the leaderboards.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.metaDescription: The terms for using POPS (“More than just sport”): accounts, content, the licence for your contributions, moderation, notices and liability.
Terms.intro: These terms govern the use of POPS (“More than just sport”). Browsing the map needs no account; by signing in you accept these terms. How we process your personal data is described separately under <privacy>Privacy</privacy>.

who.title: Who we are
who.body: POPS is run by a non-profit association:

service.title: The service
service.body: POPS is a free map of the publicly accessible sports facilities in Bulgaria, with group sessions, a sports passport, leaderboards and open data. There are no paid features. We may change, temporarily suspend or discontinue parts of the service, including for maintenance.

account.title: Your account
account.body: You sign in with your email address and a one-time code. The account is personal: do not share it and do not create one in someone else's name. You are responsible for what is done from your account and for access to your email. You can delete your account at any time from <profile>My profile</profile>.
account.age: We have not set a minimum age for an account; our age policy is under review.

content.title: What may be published
content.body: You are responsible for what you add: facility data, photos, the name and city in your profile, session titles and descriptions. Do not publish:

items.people: photos in which people can be recognised;
items.falseData: facility data you know to be false;
items.rights: content you have no rights to.

licence.title: Licence for your contributions
licence.data: The facility data you add — location, type, access, condition and more — becomes part of the POPS database, which we publish as <openData>open data</openData> under the Open Database License 1.0 (ODbL) together with the OpenStreetMap data. By submitting it you agree to it being published on those terms.
licence.photos: Photos are not part of the open data. By uploading a photo you confirm that you took it or have the right to share it and that no person can be recognised in it, and you grant us a free, non-exclusive, perpetual right to store it, process it (for example to strip its metadata and resize it) and show it on POPS. The copyright stays yours.

moderation.title: How we moderate
moderation.how: New facilities appear on the map straight away — before another member or a moderator has checked them. Photos are published only after a moderator approves them. Moderators are the volunteer ambassadors for their municipality and the POPS administrators. Automated checks can only prompt — a person always decides.
moderation.reasons: When we reject or take down your photo or remove a facility you added, we email you what we decided, on what ground — a breach of these terms or illegal content — and how to contest the decision.
moderation.restrictions: We may refuse, edit or remove content that breaks these terms or the law. For serious or repeated breaches we may restrict or close the account.

notices.title: Notices and appeals
notices.body: Anyone can tell us about content they consider illegal or in breach of these terms through the <form>notice form</form>. We handle notices promptly; if you leave an email address, we confirm receipt and tell you the decision.
notices.contest: If you disagree with a moderation decision — about your content or on your notice — write to the address on the <contact>Contact</contact> page and a person will review the decision. You may also go to court.
notices.point: Our point of contact under Articles 11 and 12 of the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065) — for authorities and for users — is the address on the <contact>Contact</contact> page. Write to us in Bulgarian or English.

accuracy.title: Accuracy of the data and liability
accuracy.body: Facility data comes from OpenStreetMap, from municipalities and from members. It may be incomplete, out of date or wrong — including whether a facility is free, lit or in good condition. Check on site before relying on it.
accuracy.risk: POPS does not own or maintain the facilities and is not responsible for their condition. You play at your own risk. As far as the law allows, we are not liable for damage arising from the use of the site or of its data.

privacy.title: Personal data
privacy.body: How and why we process your personal data, and what your rights are, is described under <privacy>Privacy</privacy>.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.body: We may change these terms. The new version is published on this page with the date from which it applies. If you do not agree with a change, you can delete your account.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: Bulgarian law applies. Disputes are settled by the competent Bulgarian court, without limiting your rights as a consumer.
